title: Equality transport of one derived unit on inverse-image opens
statement: Let h:X→Y, U an open of Y, V=h⁻¹U, g=h|U, jX:V→X and jY:U→Y. Assume the derived module categories of X, Y and their opens exist as in [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-canonical-data]. For every homotopy object K on V, let η(s,t,K) denote the composite unit with successive-image source [def-pc-direct-image-composition-unit-source], and let δ=Qh.map(β₀(K)) be its localized homotopy comparison [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-open-counit-model]. Then η(jX,h,K) followed by the equality comparison R(jX≫h)→R(g≫jY) equals δ(K) followed by η(g,jY,K). This involves one composite unit on each side, and neither chosen derived composition comparison nor pasted individual units.

proof.text: The pushforwardComp maps are sectionwise identities. pushforwardCongr identifies with equality transport along jX≫h=g≫jY by equality induction and the section formulas. Passing to complexes and the homotopy quotient shows that the displayed homotopy comparison is the equality map on direct-image objects. Quotient surjectivity treats every homotopy object.

proof.text: For a varying scheme morphism v, the derived functor and its unit are families in v. Equality induction on two equal values of v gives the unit naturality square. Qh preserves equality maps. Substitute the preceding homotopy identification and the concrete composite-unit definition. Zero complexes, empty schemes and identity morphisms require no separate hypotheses.
